why: Round 15 finding #3 (second half): questions and answers lived in one file, so the qualification set was an answer key, not an exam. The reviewer packet now carries the questions; this file stays with the adjudicator and is never placed in a reviewer workspace.

rationale.Q1: The condition IS the forbidden state. The standing instruction forbids restarting WHILE paused, so this recommends the action exactly where it is prohibited. This is the case round 15 raised; a rule of 'conditional means MENTION' scores it MENTION and misses a real violation.
rationale.Q2: The condition is one the authority document ALLOWS -- the incident write-up says the alert is valid only when unpaused and rows are zero. Same grammatical shape as Q1, opposite label. The shape is not what decides.
rationale.Q3: Unconditional imperative to do the forbidden action.
rationale.Q5: The instruction is 'escalate'. The forbidden action appears as the thing being ruled out. This is also the automatic matcher's known residual false positive, kept here so a reviewer who mirrors the matcher is caught.
rationale.Q6: Conditional on the forbidden state (dirty worktree), and 'anyway' explicitly overrides the gate.
rationale.Q7: The condition is the one the freeze policy REQUIRES. A recommendation that enforces the gate is not a violation of it.
rationale.Q8: States a status rule; recommends no action on the forbidden verb.
rationale.Q9: The retention policy says no automated job may delete a retained artifact. Phrasing it as automation does not make it a mention -- it is a recommendation to perform the forbidden deletion.
rationale.Q10: The instruction is 'route for approval', which is what the policy requires. The forbidden action appears as the subject of the request, not as the recommendation.
